summary: Short-lived streaming sessions reconnect storm causing elevated 5xx rate after keepalive/backpressure policy sweep
description: Issue summary: Customer reported a rapid increase in 5xx responses on streaming chat endpoints beginning 2026-03-13 10:05 UTC. The elevation coincided with a platform-wide keepalive and backpressure config sweep that rolled out a shorter keepalive deadline and more aggressive priority fallback thresholds. Impact: Multiple short-lived streaming sessions (~1-3s) observed reconnect loops that triggered apigw 502/503s and upstream runtime connection resets for the customer's tenant. Customer-visible symptoms: aborted streams, repeated client reconnects, and elevated error-rate metrics on their integration. Environment: prod-us-west, dedicated tenant for NimbleDocs with reserved capacity.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Initiate large number (~1000/min) of short streaming sessions to POST /v1/chat/stream with small payloads and immediate client disconnects
2) Observe apigw 502/503 counts and runtime connection resets in the same minute window
3) Reproduce after toggling keepalive window to 15s and enabling aggressive priority fallback policy
4) Verify increased retry attempts from client-side leading to accept-queue pressure

comments: 2026-03-13T10:20 Support - Aisha Patel: Customer reported 5xx spike at ~10:05 UTC; initial hypothesis is the keepalive change + priority fallback causing accept-queue churn. Asked for tenant logs and sample request IDs.

2026-03-13T10:38 SRE - Miguel Alvarez: Observed sudden threadpool grow-to-zero under rt-8; runtime logs show repeated GRPC connections closed during handshake. Possible link to short lived sessions and fast connection churn.
2026-03-13T11:02 Customer - NimbleDocs Support: Confirmed we saw repeated reconnects from our client SDK. We did not change our client code; spike started after Redwood announced config sweep.

2026-03-13T12:10 Engineering - Ethan Cole: Temporarily rolled back aggressive keepalive deadline in us-west to previous baseline (30s). Deployed an emergency increase to runtime gRPC threadpool min (x3). Monitoring shows 5xx rate trending down but still above baseline for some customers.

2026-03-13T13:45 Support - Aisha Patel: Notified customer of temporary rollback and asked for validation. Customer confirmed partial relief: streams succeed more often but intermittent blips remain during peak ingress bursts.
investigation_notes: Metric correlation: Timing aligns precisely with keepalive/backpressure policy sweep (change-id cfg-2026-0313-keepalive).

Accept-queue snapshots show a sawtooth pattern where short sessions create accept spikes, triggering priority fallback which closes long-lived keepalives and forces re-establish; this created a retry storm on tenants with many ephemeral streams.

Runtime observation: gRPC worker threads drop below expected min briefly during churn, causing connection resets (observed in rt-8 and rt-12). Hypothesis: runtime threadpool resizing + aggressive keepalive caused transient scheduling holes and GRPC library hit a path that closed sockets with ECONNRESET.
Customer behavior: NimbleDocs client SDK aggressively retries immediate reconnects on stream abort (backoff disabled for short sessions), amplifying the issue.
Cross refs: Linked to infra PR that applied prioritizer config (github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/587).
resolution: Hotfix applied: 1) Reverted keepalive deadline to 30s for us-west and disabled the aggressive fallback threshold while root cause is validated. 2) Increased runtime gRPC worker pool minimum and added a short stabilization window during config sweeps to prevent immediate threadpool shrink. 3) Deployed tenant-level guardrails: detect short-session reconnect storms and apply soft rate-limits per tenant to avoid accept-queue amplification. Customer workaround: NimbleDocs enabled client-side exponential backoff which reduced immediate retries. Follow-ups: engineering to add a canary gating step for keepalive/backpressure changes, add automated acceptance test that simulates high short-session churn, and add an alert for rapid accept-queue oscillation. Ticket will remain open until post-mitigation metrics show sustained baseline for 48 hours.
